title: Redwood POC weekly sync - benchmark review vs baseline provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review end-to-end benchmark results comparing Redwood to the baseline provider (BaselineCloud). Discussed latency P50/P95/P99, throughput at target QPS (150), batching and KV cache sizing, quantization effects, and VPC/network variance. Agreed to run additional P99 tail tests, kernel pinning, prefix caching experiment, and share normalized benchmark spreadsheet and security pack.

Schedule private deployment viability call if 99p tail meets SLA (tentative week of 2026-08-24)

transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-08-18 UTC | Start: 10:00 | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ellen Cho (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Astra Head ML), Daniel Lee (Astra Platform Eng), Sofia Martinez (Astra SRE), Ahmed Khan (Astra CTO)

Summary: quick pass over updated benchmarks; Redwood vs BaselineCloud. Covered tail latency, throughput ceilings, batching behavior, KV cache sizing, quantized runs, and VPC/network variance. Agreed on remediation tests and deliverables.

00:00 Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
00:07 Priya: priya here, daniel and sofia on my side, ahmed may be late.
00:12 Lena: great, marco and i will kick off. we sent the spreadsheet earlier, had a chance to skim?
00:20 Priya: yep skimmed. big picture: can redwood meet our P95/P99 at 150 qps?
00:30 Marco: we ran small (32t), med (128t), long (512t). sheet has avg token time and end-to-end numbers.
00:45 Daniel: baseline is BaselineCloud, same instance class?
00:50 Marco: yes matched gpu class and batch sizes where possible; see assumptions in sheet.
01:05 Sofia: redwood P50 looks better consistently but P99 sometimes worse on long context, any idea?
01:15 Marco: two likely causes: kv cache thrash causing memory pressure on long contexts, and our batching policy creating micro-bursts under your qps shape.
01:35 Priya: explain batching policy? we saw throughput peak but latency spike.
01:40 Marco: our runtime does continuous batching up to a small window; helps throughput but with bursty traffic it can hold short requests waiting for others. can tune window and adaptive flush.
01:55 Lena: we also tried q4 quantized profile, saved ~15% compute but dequantization adds overhead for very long sequences.
02:10 Ahmed: will q4 affect summarization quality?
02:16 Marco: small chance; recommend running your eval set, we'll include regression tests next run.
02:30 Daniel: sheet shows redwood holds 150 qps at batch 32 but P99 is 780ms for 512 tokens; baseline P99 is 720ms. why extra 60ms?
02:45 Marco: likely kernel selection for that model+seq length and baseline had warmer caches due to persistent instances. we can pin optimized kernel variant.
03:05 Priya: remediation plan to keep P99 under 800ms?
03:10 Marco: rerun with larger KV cache sizing and kernel pin, increase batching cap to 64 with adaptive flush, run 99th tail using your traces.
03:30 Priya: network egress in our VPC shows 10-20ms variance, that's a risk.
03:38 Marco: we recommend colocated endpoints or Redwood Dedicated with private networking to reduce variance; we'll add network baseline tests.
03:50 Ahmed: security — need SOC2 and KMS/HSM details before Dedicated.
03:56 Lena: noted, ellen will share security pack and SOC2 after call.
04:05 Ellen: i'll drop the architecture note for private deployment and key management integrations.
04:12 Sofia: throughput ceilings: baseline saturated at 230 qps, redwood at 260 qps. repeatable?
04:25 Marco: yes three runs, redwood's batching and kernel mix gives slightly higher throughput but sometimes increases tail; we'll attach run variance.
04:40 Daniel: for 512 token test, can you share raw logs for tail queries to inspect request shapes?
04:46 Marco: yes will share redacted logs.
04:50 Priya: can you try smaller batching window and prefix caching for repeated prompts?
04:57 Marco: prefix caching helps conversational repetition; will run that experiment.
05:05 Lena: recap: marco to run kernel pin + KV sizing + batch tuning + prefix caching tests and P99 tail runs; marco to share logs; ellen to send security docs; lena to normalize and share spreadsheet.
05:20 Ahmed: timeline workable, we'll validate with infra team; can we follow up 2026-08-25?
05:26 Lena: yes tentatively 8/25 after we have 99p numbers.
05:30 Priya: include quality/regression results for q4 runs.
05:36 Marco: will add regression eval outputs.
05:40 Daniel: last, costs - baseline quoted cheaper per token, any adjustments for Dedicated/commit?
05:47 Lena: we can provide committed estimates and a cost vs latency model; will include in spreadsheet.
05:55 Sofia: thanks.
06:00 Lena: thanks everyone. ellen will send security docs, marco will publish logs and updated runs by friday, lena will share normalized sheet by tomorrow.
06:12 Priya: thanks all.
06:15 Meeting end.
